citations.assessment: The named complete account describes the two shoemakers, their work in the marketplace, their behavior and the oath associated with them.
The 67b tradition describes creation and eating of the calf on the eve of Shabbat and calls the study “laws of creation.” The parallel 65b explicitly has Sefer Yetzirah as reported by Heilprin.
Rashi gives a calf grown to a third of its growth as one interpretation. He explicitly questions the third-born alternative in the creation narrative.
Yochanan’s unsuccessful effort and their own Eli-lineage explanation are explicit. This witness says Rabbi Chanina and Rabbi Hoshaya.
Maharsha argues for Rav in both names, citing the creation story and Yuchasin. He also reports the brothers identification; it remains a reported position.

The Rabbah entry gives the attribution to Yuchasin. Ketubot names the brothers collectively in the message and separately identifies the sages in its mules report. The identity inference is not independently established.
The source gives the accepted ruling about mules and the three named sages together. The opening text alone does not give the specific family rationale cited by Heilprin.

The argument concludes that Rabbi Yehudah is uncertain. Earlier Shmuel formulates the position differently, and the position labeled Chachamim in that unit is identified with Chananya. The scope of “the rabbis” in Heilprin’s report remains qualified.
The text preserves Hoshaya’s first-person Levite objection. Rabbi Yasa reports in the name of Rabbi Yochanan and the surrounding named speakers remain separate.
